title: Assumptions, Tautologies and Axioms

beats.vo_text: Every proof ends somewhere.
Not at the conclusion — that's where it *arrives*. I mean the other end. The first line. What is that standing on?
Because a proof is a chain of justifications, and every link cites the one before it. So follow it back.
And back.
This is not a new worry. Around the first century, a Greek sceptic named Agrippa laid out the problem in a form nobody has improved on since.
There are exactly three ways a chain of justification can end. Only three.
It runs forever. It closes into a circle. Or it stops at something asserted without proof.
Two of those are catastrophes. Let's watch them fail.
Route one: the chain never ends. Every statement is justified by an earlier one, forever.
Which sounds almost respectable — nothing is ever taken on faith. Follow it, though.
Nothing is ever established, because establishing anything would require finishing, and you never finish. You have not built a foundation. You have built a fall.
Route two: the chain closes. A is justified by B, B by C, and C — eventually — by A.
Now it terminates. It's finite. Every step is licensed.
And it proves absolutely anything you like.
Because a circle doesn't care what's inside it. It only cares that it closes.
So: two down. The third is what formal systems do, and they do it openly.
Stop the chain deliberately. Write down statements you assert without proof. Call them axioms. And then be answerable for everything they let you derive.
You do not prove an axiom. You choose it. And you inherit the consequences.
But not everything is safe to bolt into a proof system. There's a line, and it's worth seeing where it falls.
Some statements are true under every possible valuation. P or not-P. If P, and P implies Q, then Q.
There is no assignment of truth values that can make them fail. Not an unlikely one. Not a weird one. None.
Those are tautologies. And some statements are false under every valuation — contradictions. Everything else is contingent, which is to say: it depends on the world.
Now, a tautology carries no information about the world.
None. Change the climate, change the geometry, change the physical constants —
— and it does not so much as flicker.
That sounds like a criticism. It is the opposite. It is exactly why a tautology is safe to bolt into a proof system as a rule.
Because a rule that told you something about reality would be a premise in disguise — smuggled in, doing work, never declared.
The machinery must be empty. Everything you actually claim goes in the tray, where you can be held to it.
So axioms are chosen. Which raises the obvious question: can you choose whatever you like?
In nineteen oh-four, Ernst Zermelo needed one particular assumption to prove a result about ordering sets. It sounded harmless.
Given any collection of non-empty sets, you can pick one element from each.
That's it. That's the axiom of choice. Read it again and try to find something objectionable in it.
Mathematicians objected immediately and loudly, and it took twenty years to see exactly why they were right to.
Nineteen twenty-four. Stefan Banach and Alfred Tarski publish a consequence.
Take a solid sphere. Cut it into five pieces.
Move the pieces. Rotate them. Translate them. Do not stretch anything, do not add anything.
Reassemble.
Two spheres. Each the size of the one you started with. That is a theorem, and the axiom of choice is what makes it one.
So: refuse it. Throw it out.
And elsewhere in the structure, quietly, some vector spaces stop having bases.
That's the whole shape of it. There is no option here that costs nothing.
ZFC — Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory, with Choice — is the particular set of choices modern mathematics defaults to. Not because it is correct.
Because it is what almost everyone agreed to stand on.
Which brings us to the notation, and to the thing about it that everyone forgets.
Gamma proves phi. A proof is always relative to premises.
And the gamma does not evaporate once the theorem has a name.
*Theorem* means: follows from what we agreed to. The agreement is part of the result. It is not scaffolding you remove when the building is done.
Now — this is not a foundational curiosity. It is the shape of every result in machine learning, and getting it wrong will cost you.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: A learning guarantee is gamma proves phi.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: And the gamma reads something like this. The data are independent and identically distributed, from a fixed distribution. The hypothesis class is this one. The loss is bounded.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: Look at those. Every one is a claim about *your situation*. Not about mathematics.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: And now ship it.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: The distribution shifts — it always does. Inputs start arriving correlated. The loss spikes past its assumed bound.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: The model degrades. Metrics fall. And somebody says the theory doesn't work in practice.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: So check. Take the theorem apart.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: Every line still checks out. Nothing in it has moved. The theorem is exactly as true as the day it was proved.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: Gamma did.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: The theorem above it remains perfectly intact. And perfectly irrelevant.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: Which is why reading the gamma is not pedantry. It is the difference between knowing why your system failed, and believing that mathematics let you down.
beats.chapter: Every learning guarantee is a proof from premises

beats.vo_text: Next: a different foundation entirely. One where the premises are not written in a file somewhere — they're checked by a machine that will not let you forget them.
